prompt: Image 1 is a reference for the exact restrained watercolor botanical bark and leaf aesthetic, and Image 2 is a reference for the exact color and thin stems of the leaves. Draw one original transparent sprite sheet 2 by 2, four distinct broad spreading ash tree canopy sprays. Each quadrant fully isolated with transparent gutters, no part crosses a quadrant. They should fill much of their quadrant. Flat 2D botanical drawing, textured gouache and fine color pencil, detailed leaf veins. Think of four different small clusters from a mature tree, not four entire trees and not a wreath. Each cluster has 14-20 SMALL thin leaves in muted olive, blue-tinged fern green and deep pine shade, pale yellow-green tips, softly overlapping in layers, real gaps between the leaves to show an underlying bough. Natural varying clusters, soft detail, 100% transparent outside the visible leaves and stems, no glowing area around them. All tiny twig stems in each individual sprite converge to a single short anchor near the BOTTOM, with enough empty gap below it. Top left cluster leans left and horizontal, anchor near lower right; top right cluster is spreading rightwards, anchor near lower left; bottom left cluster is an upright narrow peaked fan with a centered anchor; bottom right cluster is a low wide uneven fan, anchor near lower center. The outline has no regular elliptical shape. No frame, no background, no box, no labels, no rings, no rings of white pixels, no rings around the art, no visible undergrowth or ground shadow. All art on a truly transparent PNG. These will sit behind the existing leaflets, not replace the branches of the tree.
